messages:
Jordan (support): hey team — AcmeCorp reported a spike of 429s on their prod integration starting ~09:20 UTC. Customer says it started after a release on their side but they only see ~3x normal QPS. They're mostly hitting /v1/chat and embeddings routes. Can SRE help attribute whether this is tenant-level quota or per-route burst?

Marcus (sre): looking. quick checks — searching ingress logs for customer_id=acme_corp and status=429. if we see `route_id` or `model` tags we can tell where throttles are applied. can you paste a sample request header or request_id?

Jordan (support): pasted in DM: headers include x-customer-id: acme_corp, route: /v1/chat, model: gpt-large, x-request-id: req-9f2. Also they hit an embeddings route concurrently to same account.

Marcus (sre): ok running a quick ES query: `customer_id:acme_corp AND status:429 AND @timestamp:[now-2h TO now]` — initial result: 1.2k 429s concentrated 09:20–09:30. Fields: route:/v1/chat (60%), route:/v1/embeddings (35%), other (5%).

Marcus (sre): from logs it looks like 429s are returned by the quota-service, not the runtime. field `quota_grant` is `false` in the hits. that implies customer-level quota exhausted or burst control triggered before runtime.

Priya (eng-platform): can you show the quota key in the logs (e.g., quota_key or pool_id)? we tag by `quota_scope: tenant:<customer_id>` or `route:<route_id>` depending on rule.

Marcus (sre): found it — `quota_scope: tenant:acme_corp`, `pool_id:reserved_tier_1`, `policy:steady_burst`. So tenant-level steady burst policy hit.

Aisha (acct rep, AcmeCorp): that surprises them — they have a reserved capacity contract but expected higher burst. They pushed a canary that sends 6 concurrent streams with larger context length.

Jordan (support): note from customer: increased max_tokens per request from 512->2048 during canary. that could raise token consumption.

Marcus (sre): yeah tokens matter because our quota is token-weighted for some tiers. two quick attribution checks we do: 1) tokens over time by customer, 2) requests per second by route/model. sample Prometheus queries: 
- tokens: `sum(rate(serving_tokens_consumed_total{customer="acme_corp"}[1m])) by (customer)`
- requests: `sum(rate(http_requests_total{customer="acme_corp", status!~"5.."}[1m])) by (route,model)`
run those around the window.

Marcus (sre): I ran the token query — token rate shot from ~12k tokens/s to ~78k tokens/s at 09:19. request QPS only rose ~3x. so increased token-per-request explains the exhaustion.

Priya (eng-platform): what about attribution to model vs route? add `model` to the vector: `sum(rate(serving_tokens_consumed_total{customer="acme_corp"}[1m])) by (customer,model,route)` — that'll tell if one model consumed most tokens.

Marcus (sre): did that — `gpt-large` is 92% of the extra token consumption. embeddings request token cost is low but they ran a short synchronous batch causing small extra QPS.

Jordan (support): customer-facing repro steps to share: 1) run their canary payload with long context and 6 concurrent streams, 2) observe 429s returned after ~2 minutes. Anything to give them to reduce impact?

Marcus (sre): mitigation suggestions to give customer: 1) reduce max_tokens or chunk inputs, 2) add client-side rate limiting (smooth bursts), 3) request a temporary bump / adjust reserved burst window with acct team. For platform fixes: consider allowing higher short-lived burst for reserved_tier_1 when token-per-request is high — but needs guardrails.

Priya (eng-platform): from observability side I'll add a dashboard panel and an alert:
- Dashboard: "Tenant throttle drilldown" with filters: customer_id, time range. panels: token rate (by model/route), request QPS, 429 rate, quota_grant=false hits, and avg tokens/request.
- Kibana/Logs panel: top request_ids returning 429 with full request header capture.
- Alert rule (prometheus): `expr = increase(quota_denied_total{reason="quota_exhausted", customer="acme_corp"}[5m]) > 10` for a customer-specific burn.

Marcus (sre): also add an alert for sudden token-rate increase vs baseline: `expr = (sum(rate(serving_tokens_consumed_total{customer=~".+"}[5m])) by (customer)) / (avg_over_time(sum(rate(serving_tokens_consumed_total{customer=~".+"}[5m])) by (customer)[1d:5m])) > 3` — fires when current token rate > 3x daily baseline. then route to support and platform.

Jordan (support): can you paste the exact Kibana saved search filter we used? customer may ask us to audit all 429s in the window.

Marcus (sre): saved search: `customer_id: "acme_corp" AND status:429 AND quota_grant:false` -> columns: @timestamp, request_id, route, model, tokens_consumed, policy, pool_id, user_agent. exportable CSV.

Priya (eng-platform): instrumentation note for long-term: ensure every log emits `tokens_consumed` and `billing_tokens` and `quota_scope` tags. we should also add `max_tokens_requested` for easier attribution.

Aisha (acct rep, AcmeCorp): for next steps from our side: we'll temporarily roll back the canary and throttle client concurrency. Also requesting a one-off burst increase for today while we rework prompts.

Jordan (support): noted — I'll route the one-off request to sales/ops with the ticket link and attach the CSV.

Marcus (sre): summary for internal ops playbook (copying here so support can paste to cust):
1) Confirm whether 429 originates from quota-service (quota_grant:false) vs runtime (429 from model runtime).
2) Query tokens and QPS by customer/model/route during window. PromQL snippets above.
3) Kibana saved search `customer_id: "<id>" AND status:429` to export request-level evidence.
4) If token-rate spike: ask customer for max_tokens and concurrency, suggest chunking or lower max_tokens.
5) If QPS spike but tokens small: check per-route rate limits or burst windows and consider temporary quota adjustment.
6) For reserved customers: check `pool_id` and contract burst policy (`steady_burst` vs `elastic_burst`).
7) File follow-up: instrument missing fields if any, add tenant drilldown dashboard, create baseline token-rate alert.

Priya (eng-platform): I'm going to create the dashboard and the Prometheus alert in the next sprint. tagging infra and billing to review token-weighted quota docs.

Jordan (support): thanks. Aisha — sharing this with the customer and closing the immediate escalation once they confirm canary rollback. :thumbsup:

Aisha (acct rep, AcmeCorp): confirmed rollback at 09:45 UTC, 429s stopped. thanks for the quick triage.

InfraBot: deployment notice — created monitoring dashboard `tenant-throttle-drilldown-acme_corp` (private)

Marcus (sre): closing notes: root cause = token-weighted tenant quota exhausted due to higher tokens/request during their canary. action items: customer to reduce tokens/rollback (done), acct to handle temporary bump if needed, platform to add dashboard and alerts, add better logging of `max_tokens_requested`.

Jordan (support): closing thread — will reopen if anything else comes up.
